preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is a positive integer.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) and len(s) == M and all(c in '01' for c in s) for s in [row_str, col_str])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the row string (length M) and column string (length N) consist only of '0' and '1' characters.
The number of queries Q is a positive integer.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= N and 1 <= y <= M for x, y in queries)
preconditions.description: For every query (x, y), the coordinates satisfy 1 <= x <= N and 1 <= y <= M.
The sum of N, M, and Q over all test cases does not exceed 10^6.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line) == Q and all(c in '01' for c in line) for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is a string of length Q consisting only of '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[t][k] == '1' if (win_state(row_str, col_str, x, y) == 'Alice') else '0' for t in range(T) for k, (x, y) in enumerate(queries_list[t]))
postconditions.description: For each test case t and query k with position (x, y), the k-th character of the t-th output line is '1' if Alice wins starting from (x, y), and '0' if Bob wins. The win state is determined by the game rules: a player moving to (0, i) loses if row_str[i-1] is '1' (otherwise wins), and moving to (i, 0) loses if col_str[i-1] is '1' (otherwise wins). The winner is determined by optimal play from the initial position.
